neighbours.label: Fires on geological-process vocabulary in earth-science text (volcanic eruptions, geological processes, plate movement, deep-time dates of eruptions), not on chemistry or biology processes or on fossils in a museum setting.
fire: The island was built up by repeated volcanic eruptions over many thousands of years.
Granite forms deep underground through slow geological processes of cooling.
The Himalayas are still rising because of plate collisions beneath them.
These basalt layers record volcanic activity that lasted almost a million years.
Geologists study how tectonic plates drift a few centimetres each year.
The canyon walls show several geological episodes of uplift and erosion.
Massive volcanic outpourings about 250 million years ago may have caused the extinction.
Hot springs in the valley are fed by volcanic heat from below.
quiet: The island was built up by repeated waves of settlers over many hundreds of years.
Cheese forms slowly through biological processes of fermentation.
The prices are still rising because of supply problems in the region.
These old letters record family life that lasted almost a century.
Economists study how interest rates drift a few points each year.
The novel shows several emotional episodes in the hero's childhood.
The museum's dinosaur hall reopened after a long renovation.
Hot meals in the canteen are paid for by the school board.
